name: HHC - Operations Platform
desc:
Please review the Aug 31 deep-dive call before estimation. Emma walked us through the current CareStitch, BambooHR, Google Sheets and QuickBooks workflows in detail.

**Phase 1 should remain an internal centralized operations platform for HHC office staff and clinicians. Do not include the EHR/EMR build in Phase 1.**

**Deliverables:**

**1. Internal Roadmap**

1. **UserFlow Diagram. Separate Diagrams for Phase 1 and Phase 2**

### Phase 1 – Core Scope

1. **Referral / CareStitch Replacement**

- Create patient/referral records
- Capture agency, patient, MRN/identifier, contact, referral type, discipline, insurance info, notes, etc.
- Clinician coverage areas by ZIP code/polygon
- Match referrals primarily by location
- Referral distribution to eligible clinicians
- First-come-first-served acceptance
- Admin manual assignment/override
- Track pending, assigned, closed/unstaffed referrals
- Clinicians should be able to accept referrals from both mobile-responsive web and desktop

1. **Communication**

- HIPAA-compliant patient-specific chat
- Admin team automatically included based on team/role
- Clinician added once assigned
- Ability to create configurable department channels such as HR, billing, intake, medical records
- General announcements / direct communication as needed

1. **User Roles**

- Admin/manager
- Office staff
- Clinician
- Different permissions and visibility by role
- Clinicians only see assigned patients/chats
- Admin can access broader patient/referral activity

1. **Clinician Credential / HR Module**

BambooHR is currently used mostly for credentials, not payroll.

- Clinician onboarding checklist
- Credential/document uploads
- Expiration dates
- Automated renewal reminders
- Admin tracking
- Credential compliance status
- Alert/block new referrals when required credentials are expired, subject to admin override
- Agency-controlled access to relevant clinician credentials should be explored

1. **Visit Tracking**

- Clinicians should record/confirm completed visits within the platform
- Remove dependency on separate clinician Google billing sheets
- Track visit date, agency, patient, visit type, documentation status, etc.
- Clinician should have visibility into completed visits

1. **Clinician Payables**

Important: HHC has separate clinician and agency rate structures.

- Each clinician can have different rates by visit type
- System should calculate what HHC owes the clinician
- Clinician should ideally see earnings/payout information

1. **Agency Billing**

- Each agency has contracted rates by visit type
- Agency rate may differ from clinician rate
- Support manual exceptions, e.g. additional $50 for an urgent referral
- Generate cleaned billing data automatically
- Direct QuickBooks integration is NOT required initially
- A QuickBooks-compatible Excel/CSV export is acceptable

1. **Reporting**

Highest-priority report is the current Visit Request Report:

- Referrals received
- Staffed vs unstaffed
- By city / geography
- By agency
- Referral outcome
- Clinician acceptance/activity where useful

Emma currently manipulates this manually to identify coverage gaps, e.g. high referral volume in cities where HHC cannot staff patients.

### Phase 2 – Keep Separate

Do **not** include the following in Phase 1 estimation:

- Custom centralized EHR/EMR
- AI-assisted clinical documentation
- Agency QA portal for notes
- Clinical note correction workflow
- PDF clinical-note export
- Geotagging/live location
- Patient digital signatures
- EHR integrations/interoperability
- HL7/FHIR integration work

name: CTLG - Workflow Automation
desc:
CTLG Consulting is a growing education consulting business working with 50+ school divisions and ~25 independent contractors.

Their current operations are managed through Google Workspace, Google Sheets, Calendar, email, and QuickBooks. The main pain point is keeping track of the workflow after a proposal is agreed, including contractor assignment, scheduling, reminders, delivery checkpoints, client follow-up, invoicing, and payment tracking.

They do not need proposal generation itself automated. The opportunity is to automate the proposal-to-invoice workflow while keeping their existing Google-based setup.

Please do not estimate for a full end to end platform. This can be done via automations .

Key automation opportunities:

- When a proposal is approved, create/update an engagement record automatically.
- Trigger contractor assignment workflow based on service/date required.
- Check shared calendar availability for core contractors and send availability requests to others.
- Create confirmed calendar events once a contractor is assigned.
- Send automatic reminders before each engagement.
- Trigger post-engagement reminders for consultant deliverables/feedback.
- Mark an engagement complete once required follow-up is done.
- Flag completed engagements as invoice-ready.
- Push invoice data into QuickBooks or create an invoice task automatically.
- Track unpaid invoices and surface overdue items.
- Maintain one dashboard showing client, contractor, dates, engagement status, deliverables, and invoice/payment status.

Recommended direction:
Use their existing Google ecosystem where possible, potentially Apps Script / AppSheet / Make or Zapier + QuickBooks API, instead of replacing everything with custom software.

Potential Phase 1:

- Proposal / engagement tracking
- Contractor assignment and availability
- Calendar and email reminders
- Delivery milestone tracking
- Invoice-ready workflow
- QuickBooks integration
- Simple operations dashboard

name: (E) Sentinel Midstream - Texas GulfLink Crude Terminal Planning Model
desc:
We need an estimate for the **full roadmap**, broken into phases so the client can see the cost and timeline for the immediate planning tool as well as the eventual operational system.

### Phase 1 - Planning / Feasibility Tool

Target is Q4 2026. This will be used while Sentinel is negotiating with crude suppliers and customers.

Estimate for:

- Tank capacities and operating constraints
- Pipeline capacities and flow-rate constraints
- Environmental/permit throughput limits
- Crude grades and basic quality properties
- RVP/blending calculations using assumed values
- Supplier nominations including volume, delivery window and rate
- Expected vessel demand/loading schedules
- Inventory and tank allocation modeling
- Feasibility testing across all constraints
- Detailed flags showing where and why a scenario fails
- Recommendations for schedule adjustments where possible
- Scenario modeling
- Schedule/output generation
- Simple internal interface for entering assumptions and reviewing results

The main Phase 1 question is: **Given expected receipts and vessel demand, can Sentinel move enough crude through the pipelines and tanks without violating physical, inventory, blending or permit constraints?**

### Phase 2 - Operational Scheduling Platform

This is the eventual production system Sentinel would use when the terminal becomes operational.

Estimate separately for:

- Monthly nomination management
- Automated schedule optimization
- Incoming and outgoing movement scheduling
- Actual vs planned movement updates
- Re-optimization when receipts or vessels are delayed
- Live tank inventory and crude-quality data
- Sensor/SCADA integration
- Actual RVP values and operational blending calculations
- Tank/customer-specific blend management
- User roles and permissions
- Historical data/reporting
- Audit trail
- Operational alerts/constraint violations
- Production-grade web application
- Relevant external system integrations

No mobile app is currently required.

Cloud can be assumed for estimation, but the client has not finalized cloud vs on-prem for the eventual operational system.

Please provide **effort, team composition, timeline and cost for each phase separately**, along with the combined roadmap and total estimate.

Clearly call out assumptions, especially around SCADA/sensor integrations or other systems where APIs/technical details are not yet available.

Please review the recordings in the Drive for the complete requirements and business context before finalizing the estimate.

name: (H) Theranostics - Data Aggregation
desc:
### **Background**

Discovery call with **Zach Levko** to explore potential areas of collaboration between National Nephrology Alliance and PureLogics.

Zach explained that National Nephrology Alliance supports and operates nephrology practices by managing many of their administrative and back-office functions. These include front desk operations, medical assistants, billing and collections, and care coordination teams. Their practices are high volume (approximately **25,000 patient visits annually** at one of their clinics) and operate on a combination of **Athena** and **Epic** systems, with additional EMRs used across affiliated oncology practices.

The conversation initially focused on manual workflows within billing and collections, particularly prior authorizations, denials management, and claims processing. Zach shared that while reducing billing costs remains an important long-term objective, he believes another opportunity offers a faster path to demonstrating value.

---

### **Primary Opportunity**

Develop an AI-assisted solution to automate **clinical data aggregation from patient records**.

Current workflow:

- Pharmaceutical companies engage Zach's organization to provide datasets for research-related initiatives.
- A typical request involves identifying approximately **100 qualifying patients** and extracting around **20 predefined data elements** for each patient.
- The required information is often spread across structured EMR fields and unstructured physician notes, making extraction difficult.
- Medical assistants currently perform this work manually by opening each patient chart, reviewing documentation, identifying the requested information, and compiling it into the required dataset.
- Zach believes this manual review process could potentially be automated through AI capable of understanding patient records and extracting the required information.

He also mentioned two related future opportunities:

- Identifying patients who meet **clinical trial eligibility** criteria.
- Identifying patients who may qualify for **specific therapeutic treatments** based on clinical information.

However, he stated that **data aggregation is the highest-priority opportunity** because it already aligns with existing contracts and provides the quickest path to demonstrating business value.

---

### **Current Environment**

**Nephrology Operations**

- One primary location currently uses **Athena**.
- Other nephrology locations utilize an **Epic-based** system.
- Heavy administrative workload driven by prior authorizations, claims management, and denial processing.

**Oncology Operations**

- Approximately **25 oncology practices** are supported.
- These practices collectively use an estimated **5–8 different EMRs**.
- Zach believes the initial project could be completed using data from approximately **five clinics**, covering roughly **three different EMRs**, before expanding to additional systems.

---

### **Support Required**

We need a **Solutions Architect/technical resource** to lead a deeper discovery session focused on the **data aggregation opportunity**.

The objective of the session is to:

- Gain a detailed understanding of the client's current data extraction workflow.
- Identify how patient data is currently stored and accessed across the different EMRs.
- Understand the specific data points the pharmaceutical companies request and where they typically reside (structured fields vs. clinical notes).
- Clarify integration requirements, technical constraints, and assumptions.
- Gather enough information to prepare a high-level solution approach, timeline, and estimate for the initial proof-of-concept.

The client has already confirmed that **data aggregation is their highest-priority use case** and would like to understand our technical approach, implementation process, expected timeline, and high-level costing. The purpose of this call is to collect the technical information needed before moving into estimation.

name: MSL Healthcare - J A
desc:
### 1. **Client Background**

MSL Healthcare Ltd. is a UK-based healthcare staffing company operating under multiple sister businesses (Healthcare, Education, and MLS). The current discussion pertains **only to the Healthcare division**, which manages recruitment, timesheets, and payroll for healthcare professionals.

The company’s existing backend system relies heavily on **Eclipse**, an outdated, legacy database system with no automation or integration capabilities. Payroll operations and timesheet processing are extremely manual, resulting in high administrative overhead and inefficiency.

---

### 2. **Problem Statement**

The client’s current operations are **highly manual, error-prone, and time-consuming** due to dependency on the Eclipse system.

Key pain points include:

- Manual entry of contracts and timesheets (300–400 entries weekly).
- Every shift and nurse contract must be input individually.
- High risk of data errors (a single incorrect checkbox can block processing).
- Time-consuming approval and authorization workflows.
- No integration between **Eclipse** (operational system) and **Sage** (accounting software).
- Payroll data is outsourced to umbrella companies, further complicating workflows.
- Limited reporting capabilities and lack of process visibility.

In short, **MSL Healthcare’s operational efficiency is constrained by outdated software and fragmented workflows**, preventing scalability and increasing administrative cost.

---

### 3. **Project Objective**

To **replace Eclipse** with a modern, scalable, and easy-to-use software platform that:

- Automates contract, timesheet, and payroll workflows.
- Integrates seamlessly with **Sage** accounting.
- Reduces manual intervention and admin time.
- Ensures data accuracy and process transparency.
- Provides reporting and dashboard capabilities for management oversight.

---

### 4. **Functional Requirements (Initial Scope)**

#### A. **Core Modules**

1. **Contract Management**
   - Digital creation, storage, and tracking of staff contracts.
   - Quick input or import of contract details (e.g., nurse, shift, pay rate, dates).
   - Validation rules to prevent incorrect entries.
2. **Timesheet Management**
   - Automated collection (via email, upload, or web portal).
   - Approval workflow (consultant → manager → payroll).
   - Integration with contract data for validation.
   - Error-handling and status tracking (pending, approved, rejected).
3. **Payroll & Invoicing**
   - Automated calculation of payments from approved timesheets.
   - Support for outsourcing model (umbrella companies).
   - Integration with **Sage** for posting payroll/invoice data.
   - Option for weekly or bi-weekly payment cycles.
4. **Integration Layer**
   - Bi-directional or one-way sync with **Sage** (configurable).
   - Secure data handling and audit trail.
5. **Reporting & Analytics**
   - Standard reports: Timesheet summary, consultant activity, payroll summary, invoice aging.
   - Dashboard with key operational KPIs (time-to-process, payments pending, etc.).

---

### 5. **Non-Functional Requirements**

- **Usability:** Intuitive, modern UI; easy for non-technical staff.
- **Performance:** Handle 400–500 contracts and timesheets weekly without latency.
- **Scalability:** Modular design for future addition of Education or Staffing divisions.
- **Security & Compliance:** GDPR-compliant data handling; role-based access control.
- **Deployment Preference:** Cloud-based (pending client confirmation).
- **Integrations:** Primary target – Sage
- The client is **open to platform suggestions** (custom build vs. hybrid

---

### 7. **Deliverables (for internal team)**

By next meeting, we need:

1. **Solution options** (e.g., custom build vs. integration-first approach).
2. **Technical architecture overview** (modules + data flow).
3. **Proposed tech stack** (consider modern, low-maintenance options).
4. **Integration plan** with Sage (possible API or connector use).
5. **Implementation timeline** (phased delivery recommendation).

desc:
**Client Pain Point:** Doug has been burned by Meta ads and cold outreach tools that promised leads but delivered almost no orders. His growth currently depends on Google Ads and the ASI distributor network, both of which have a natural ceiling. He has the capacity to double his business but no scalable way to find qualified buyers.

**Client Requirement:** Doug needs a system that finds businesses already looking for custom branded water, not cold unaware prospects. He wants a ranked, ready-to-contact lead list delivered to his team on a regular basis. He wants to start small, prove results, and scale from there.

## Shoreline Credit Union – Technical Planning

Tauqeer was on the technical scoping call with Shoreline Credit Union on August 17 and gathered/validated the requirements directly with the client.

### What we need

Please coordinate with **Tauqeer** and prepare the following:

1. **Internal Roadmap**
   - Create a phased technical roadmap based on the requirements gathered by Tauqeer.
   - This is primarily for internal planning and estimation.
   - Clearly separate the initial POC from future/production phases.
2. **Client-Facing User Flow Diagram**
   - Create a simple user flow showing how the proposed solution would work from the user's perspective.
   - Tauqeer should be able to walk the client through this on the next call.
   - Keep this business-friendly and avoid unnecessary technical detail.
3. **Architecture Diagram**
   - Create a technical architecture showing the proposed components, document processing/AI layer, data flow, integrations, security considerations, and human review points.
   - This is mainly for internal use but should be presentable if Shoreline brings a technical stakeholder onto the next call.

### Brief Solution Overview

Shoreline wants to explore an **AI-powered document review and workflow solution for its credit union operations**.

The primary use case is **loan file review**. Today, an employee manually reviews roughly **50–60 consumer loan packets per month**, with vehicle loans being the main focus. The solution should analyze PDF loan packets for missing documents/pages, unchecked boxes, signatures, initials, dates, incorrect or inconsistent information, and other checklist/policy issues.

There is also a **DTI validation use case**, where the system should pull relevant debts from the credit report and compare them against standardized income information to identify calculation errors or threshold issues.

Findings should be presented to a human reviewer with the relevant document/page/field and then routed back to the **loan officer** for correction. Final loan acceptance, policy exceptions, and credit decisions remain human-controlled.

A secondary use case is **Accounts Payable automation**, covering approximately **100–150 invoices/month**. The system would extract invoice information, validate it, flag duplicates/errors, suggest coding, and route invoices for approval.

Their core/accounting platform is **Jack Henry Symitar**, with API integrations potentially required.

Shoreline is currently evaluating **build vs. buy**, so the immediate goal is to give them a clear picture of what a PureLogics-built solution would look like and how we would approach the POC.

## **Project Requirements Document – Highland Cabinetry Inc. (Secondary E-Commerce Website)**

_Muhammad Umair Naseem - was with me on this call - so please loop him in solution prep as well._

### **Goal**

- Create a public-facing online store for cabinetry products with advanced e-commerce features and strong SEO performance.

---

### **Reference Websites**

1. [**buywholesalecabinetry.com**](https://buywholesalecabinets.com/?srsltid=AfmBOoo4-M1f5u4EfGyWoQszFaV0sKxCdS96oQyfkQi01J2N1FMcNtBv "‌")

These websites should serve as **functional and design references**.

> James stated: “I want to base mine off of theirs with all the functionality, arguably better if possible.”

---

### **Core Functional Requirements**

#### **1. Product Catalog**

- Approximately **275 parent SKUs**.
- A few **thousand sub-SKUs** under them (e.g., same cabinet in multiple colors).
- Example: One base 18-inch cabinet available in blue, black, white, gray.
- System must support hierarchical product structure (Parent SKU → Variants).

#### **2. E-Commerce Workflow**

- Customers should be able to **browse, select, and purchase** cabinetry directly.
- Website should be **user-friendly** and **simple to navigate**.
- The site must be designed to **handle high traffic and large transaction volumes** (e.g., 100–200 orders per day).

#### **3. 3D Rendering / Design Tool**

- For **homeowners and do-it-yourselfers**.
- Users should be able to **input measurements** (e.g., 10ft x 5ft kitchen).
- Tool should **visualize the kitchen layout** using selected cabinets.
- Should **suggest designs or layouts** automatically based on input dimensions.
- The goal is to allow users to “see” their kitchen virtually.

#### **4. Portals and Roles**

- **Customer Portal:**
  - Register/log in.
  - Customize their kitchen.
  - View and manage orders.
  - Use 3D rendering tools.
- **Admin Portal:**
  - Manage customers, products, and SKUs.
  - Monitor website activity (e.g., traffic, top-used SKUs).
  - Handle business analytics.
- **User Roles:**
  - Approximately **5–10 different roles** expected, including:
    - Admin
    - Customer
    - Vendor (limited access)
    - Freight specialist
    - IT staff
    - SEO specialist
  - (James clarified he was referring to _types of users_, not user count.)

#### **5. Vendor Management**

- Vendors will **not** have control or management privileges on the website.
- Vendor data should sync via **ERP integration**:
  - Either through an **API connection** to the ERP (preferred).
  - Or via **daily inventory file uploads**.
- No separate vendor portal for operations.
- Optional (low priority): potential vendor **portfolio feature** (for future), where vendors could showcase previous work, but James marked this as _low priority_.

#### **6. ERP Integration**

- The website must connect with backend **ERP systems** to:
  - Retrieve **inventory and stock levels**.
  - Support **multi-vendor** data (if required in the future).
- Integration method: **API or file-based sync**.

#### **7. Technology & Platform**

- Current Highland website is on **WordPress**, but the new one may use a different stack.
- **No fixed technology preference** stated by the client.
- Open to recommendations for both:
  - **Platform/framework choice**, and
  - **Plugins/tools** for specific functions (e.g., 3D rendering).
- **Key requirement:** Must be _highly scalable, stable under high traffic_, and _user-friendly_.
- **Performance expectations:**
  - Load balancing should be implemented.
  - System should not crash under heavy concurrent usage.
- **AI Integration:**
  - Team member (Muhammad) suggested possible use of **Python and AI** for 3D rendering/customization.
  - James did **not** request AI specifically but was open to efficient technical solutions.

#### **8. SEO & Marketing**

- **Very high priority.**
- Website must be designed for **strong SEO performance**.
- Full **flexibility and control over SEO elements** (meta tags, URLs, schema, etc.).
- Must allow integration with marketing and analytics tools.
- Client runs an SEO company and plans to manage optimization internally.
- Client emphasized: “That’s my hesitation with Shopify — I want to make sure I can fully control SEO.”

---

### **9. Design Expectations**

- Must be **beautiful and modern**.
- **User-friendly interface** and **easy navigation** are critical.
- Should visually compete with or surpass the reference sites.

---

### **10. Traffic and Load Expectations**

- High-volume site expected (100–200 orders per day).
- Must support **heavy concurrent traffic** without degradation.
- Load balancing and performance optimization are required.

---

### **11. Project Timeline**

- **Target Launch Date:** **January 1st.**
- **Follow-up Meeting:** Next Wednesday (same time) for review of solution proposal.

name: Minerva Medical  - L
desc:
# Problem Statement

Minerva Medical Group requires a **secure, cloud-based health risk assessment system** that accepts health-related survey responses containing personal health information (PHI), runs those responses through a defined algorithm, and produces environmental hazard **risk scores**. The system must support multiple client sites, provide role-based access and auditability, be maintainable and scalable, and be hosted on Azure with HIPAA compliance considerations. Luke will provide the algorithm structure and other detailed inputs needed to implement scoring and outputs.

---

# Requirements (strictly as discussed)

## 1. Functional Requirements — Survey & Data

- Support creation and intake of health-related **survey responses** (the number of questions and exact content to be provided by Luke).
- Store survey responses tied to individual users/logins.
- Allow survey responses to be processed by the algorithm supplied by the client to generate a **risk score**.
- Allow users to query the system with different environmental conditions to receive corresponding risk scores based on the stored survey response.

## 2. Algorithm & Outputs

- Implement the algorithm structure and scoring logic that Luke will provide (algorithm structure, number of questions, risk scoring output details).
- Store risk score outputs in a retrievable format (output format preferences to be confirmed by Luke).
- Allow re-running or applying the algorithm for different environmental condition inputs against existing survey data.

## 3. User Roles & Access

- **End users** must have individual logins and be able to complete surveys and view their own results.
- A **supervisor** role on the client side must be able to view retrieval logs (audit of who accessed data and when) but must **not** be able to view the underlying algorithm.
- Support administrative/system roles for support and maintenance activities (details to be handled in internal planning).

## 4. Security & Compliance

- Host the platform in **Microsoft Azure** and ensure the hosting and architecture address **HIPAA** compliance for handling PHI (specific Azure setup details to be provided by the solution team and agreed with Luke).
- Ensure PHI is protected and that access is auditable as discussed.

## 5. Data Volume & Scalability

- Anticipated initial usage: **12–20 users per site** and **12–30 data entries per week** (per site).
- The system must support these initial volumes and be designed with scalability in mind for future growth.

## 6. User Interface & Development Approach

- Deliver a **simple, test-friendly UI** first to facilitate testing and adjustments by Luke’s team.
- Develop the UI and algorithm backend in parallel, per the discussion.

## 7. Database / Long-Term Storage

- The database design must support building tables that establish relationships between survey answers, environmental conditions, and risk scores (Luke and Zukhruf discussed building out these tables).
- Include consideration for long-term data storage and retrieval/archiving (client raised long-term storage concerns to be addressed).

I need a detailed solution on this including the roadmap (excel based) and the workflow diagrams + Data base handling and choice + Information about the pricing on the hosting and the reason to choose the provider because prospect said he is comfortable with Azure, hence we need to give strong rationale if we are to suggest AWS.

name: We Advisors - T
desc:
**Problem Statement**

Financial advisors currently face significant **scalability, efficiency, and automation challenges** in managing client portfolios, tax planning, and financial advisory processes. The reliance on **spreadsheets and limited customization of third-party tools** makes the process cumbersome, error-prone, and time-consuming.

The prospect envisions a **cloud-based, automated platform** that integrates **portfolio modeling, tax planning, investment allocation, document management, and collaboration** into a seamless experience for advisors and clients. The goal is to **streamline advisory operations, reduce manual work, improve efficiency, and enhance user experience** while maintaining flexibility for different advisor approaches.

### **Core Challenges**

1. **Manual & Inefficient Data Handling:**
   - Advisors rely on spreadsheets that are prone to human error.
   - Portfolio allocation, tax planning, and financial modeling require manual entry.
   - No structured system to **track changes and maintain version history**.
2. **Fragmented Document Management:**
   - Financial plans, investment strategies, and client documents are stored in multiple locations.
   - No centralized **"Wealth Vault"** to store, organize, and share client data securely.
   - Lack of **document versioning and access control** for sub-advisors (CPAs, attorneys, etc.).
3. **Inefficient Portfolio & Investment Planning:**
   - Current allocation strategy involves **manual spreadsheet calculations**.
   - Advisors need flexibility to **customize investment buckets** but lack automation.
   - Need for **tax-aware investment allocation** to optimize returns.
4. **Limited Scalability & Advisor Productivity:**
   - Advisors handle clients one-by-one with **high time investment per client**.
   - Training new advisors is time-consuming due to lack of structured processes.
   - No standardized workflow automation for client meetings, document uploads, or task tracking.

### **Solution Requirements**

## Problem Statement

In Bangladesh, a large portion of the population — including small vendors, rickshaw pullers, and market sellers — still rely heavily on **cash transactions**. Many of these individuals do not have access to banking channels, POS machines, or digital payment infrastructure. Existing solutions (such as **bKash, Rocket, and Nagad**) are widely used but still leave gaps for easy, inclusive, and device-free transactions.

The prospect wants to address this gap by creating a **FinTech platform** that provides an **alternative to cash**, enabling simple, secure, and accessible digital transactions. The vision is to allow everyday users and small businesses to perform transactions without relying on POS machines or extensive banking setups, while also ensuring **security, simplicity, and inclusivity**.

BlackCapital is onboarding thousands of users (B2B model) at once—primarily foreign visa workers (H-2A/H-2B), undocumented immigrants, and unbanked U.S. citizens. Currently done manually by agents. They want to:

- Eliminate human involvement from the onboarding flow.

- First Name
- Last Name
- Phone Number (U.S.)
- U.S. Address
- Passport photo (upload)
- Domestic ID photo (upload) — optional: driver's license, etc.

name: Yang Di - Proposal
desc:
**Background**

Yang is the founder of [http://MediaFusion.ai](http://MediaFusion.ai "smartCard-inline")  — an AI-powered content company that produces multimedia ads and social media content for businesses. They charge clients per piece of content produced. If the content doesn't perform, clients churn. That's the core business risk.

---

**The Problem**

Their AI generates content blindly. It has no real-world feedback loop telling it what actually works. It can't distinguish between platforms (TikTok vs LinkedIn), niches (skincare vs SaaS), or audience types. The result is generic content that doesn't engage — wasted credits, unhappy clients, churn.

Three specific engineering problems they've identified:

- **Causality vs correlation** — the system can see a post performed well but can't know if it was the content structure, the author's fame, or just timing
- **True personalisation** — scraping a website gives niche-level guesses but not the real pain of a specific company
- **Algorithm uncertainty** — LinkedIn and TikTok change their ranking signals without notice and never explain why

---

**What needs to be built**

A system that continuously watches high-performing content across social platforms, analyses why it worked, and feeds those patterns back into the AI so future content is smarter and more engaging. Think of it as a self-improving content brain.

For now - we need a detailed proposal explaining how we would tackle this problem. If Yang sees the value - he would go ahead with an engineer. Please consult Ahmad Khalid as he was on the meeting

name: Baird Augustine - R
desc:
### **Problem Statement**

Baird Augustine currently manages large institutional debt deals (typically **$25 million and above**) through a manual process. Recently, they have seen a rise in smaller debt deal requests (**below $25 million**).

While these smaller transactions help build early-stage relationships with clients, they are highly **manual and time-consuming**, diverting focus from larger, more profitable deals.

The need identified during the discussion is to **automate the sub-$25 million debt deal process** — enabling efficiency, reducing manual effort, and freeing up the team’s bandwidth for high-value work.

---

### **2. Business Context**

Baird Augustine operates three main business units:

1. **Investment Banking** – Works with 33 family offices, deploying approximately $20B annually.
2. **Asymmetrical Alpha** – Hedge fund division.
3. **Focus on Risk** – Investor network hosting institutional investing events.

The automation platform will primarily support the **Investment Banking** division’s smaller-deal operations.

---

### **3. Current Workflow (Manual)**

1. Clients reach out via email or phone to request debt funding.
2. The team collects basic information manually.
3. Clients submit **bank statements**:
   - 3 months if based outside **New York or California**.
   - 4 months if based **in New York or California**.
4. An internal team member manually inputs data from the bank statements into a spreadsheet to determine the client’s debt capacity.
5. Quotes are manually requested from liquidity providers via email.
6. Once providers reply, a team member compares quotes and sends the best option to the client.
7. Deal progress is tracked manually in **Asana**.

This process is repetitive, human-dependent, and limits scalability.

---

### **4. Target Workflow (Automation Scope)**

Ryan confirmed that automation is needed only for **debt deals under $25 million**.
The **larger, complex deals** will continue to involve significant human interaction.

The automated process should begin **on Baird Augustine’s website**, allowing borrowers to self-initiate their applications online.

---

### **5. Functional Requirements (as discussed)**

#### **5.1 Client Intake Form**

- Hosted on **Baird Augustine’s website** (currently not available).
- Form to collect:
  - Loan amount range (e.g., under $5M, $5M–$10M, $10M–$25M).
  - Type of debt (e.g., Line of Credit, Supply Chain Financing, Asset-Based, Revenue-Based, SBA Loan, etc.).
- **Dynamic fields:** form expands based on user input (e.g., type of loan or business details).
- Borrowers can **upload bank statements (PDFs)** directly.
- The system should validate that clients provide:
  - 3 statements (if outside NY/CA).
  - 4 statements (if inside NY/CA).

---

#### **5.2 Data Extraction and Analysis**

- Extract relevant financial data from uploaded bank statements, including:
  - Monthly ending balances.
  - Cash inflows and outflows.
- Calculate the **debt amount the business qualifies for**, based on this extracted data.
- The goal is to replace the manual spreadsheet calculations currently done by the team.
- **Credit scoring, covenants, or financial ratio templates** may be considered later (“maybe in the future”).
- Business performance (not personal credit) should remain the key eligibility factor.

---

#### **5.3 Lender / Liquidity Provider Workflow**

- Baird Augustine works with an existing list of **liquidity providers**.
- The system should:
  - Automatically send quote requests to these providers once analysis is complete.
  - Receive and compile responses for comparison.
- A **human analyst** must still review the offers and select the best one.
- Option for manual negotiation before sending the quote to the client.

---

#### **5.4 User Roles (Defined in the Conversation)**

RoleDescription

- **Client (Borrower):** Fills the online form, uploads documents, and submits a request.
- **Internal Analyst:** Reviews system output (eligibility amount, provider quotes), validates accuracy, and communicates with the client.
- **Liquidity Provider:** Receives quote requests and sends responses (currently via email).
- **Admin (Ryan / Management)**: Oversees all processes, user permissions, and deal tracking.

---

#### **5.5 Workflow Integration**

- **Asana:**
  - Every new application should automatically create a task in Asana.
  - Tasks show deal type, amount range, and client name.
- **Google Workspace:**
  - Used for document storage and internal communication.
- **CRM:**
  - Not in use currently; no CRM integration required at this stage.

---

### **6. End-to-End Workflow (Based on Conversation)**

1. Client visits Baird Augustine’s website.
2. Client fills in the online intake form and uploads 3–4 months of bank statements.
3. System extracts and analyzes financial data.
4. System determines the maximum eligible debt amount.
5. Quote requests are sent to Baird Augustine’s listed liquidity providers.
6. Providers reply with their quotes.
7. System aggregates all quotes.
8. Analyst reviews and selects the best option (or negotiates if needed).
9. Quote is sent to the client for approval or rejection.
10. The deal is logged and tracked in **Asana**.

---

### **7. Process Rules (Confirmed in Discussion)**

- Deals **below $25 million** are the automation target.
- **Line of Credit** → fewer questions.
- **Complex debt types** → more detailed information required.
- Conditional logic within the form based on:
  - Loan amount.
  - Type of debt.
  - Borrower’s responses.
- For smaller, simpler loans (like working capital), the process can be mostly automated.
- Large, complex loans still require human intervention.

I need a complete solution on this including workflows and roadmap.

**Card Title:** Discovery Analysis: Stairway Invest (Austin Fowler)

**Description:**

**Client & Business Model Overview**

- **Client:** Austin Fowler (Stairway Invest)
- **Location:** US West Coast
- **Current Scale:** ~500 clients, 23 years in business.
- **Existing Tech Team:** Small internal team (1 Full-time, 2 Part-time).

**The Core Concept (Crucial Context)** Stairway acts as an investment education platform that offers "Savings Accounts" (legally defined as Regulation D, 506C/B personally guaranteed debt funds).

- **Value Prop:** They pay 8% APY (beating standard US banks).
- **Mechanism:** They operate on a fractional reserve model (keeping ~20% or the sum of the top 2 clients' funds in cash).
- **The Upsell:** They teach users how to invest, eventually helping them set up their _own_ debt funds (charging ~$15k in legal fees) to raise capital up to $150M.
- **Legal Note:** We cannot use the words "Bank" or "Deposit" in public copy due to SEC regulations.

**Current Platform Functionality (As-Is)**

- **User Roles:**
  1. **Investor:** Can deposit/withdraw funds (via Dwolla integration). Requires US Tax ID & Address.
  2. **Fundraiser:** Can create accounts for others, share calendar links, and raise capital.
- **Payment Gateway:** Dwolla (US Only).
- **Risk Management:** System enforces a maximum deposit limit per client to prevent "Whales" (over-concentration of risk).

**Pain Points & Scope of Work (To-Be)** Austin wants to scale from 500 clients to thousands. The current manual processes are the bottleneck.

1. **Transaction Automation (Priority)**
   - Current: Many bank accounts were added manually; transactions over a certain limit generate backend manual work for Austin.
   - Requirement: Automate the transaction process fully.
   - Constraint: Automation target is for transactions up to $50,000. Anything above that will remain manual for now.
2. **White-Labeling / "Web Skinning"**
   - Current: Platform is branded as Stairway.
   - Requirement: Build a "Portal" feature.
   - Use Case: A partner company called "Urban Genesis" needs a portal that functions like Stairway but looks like Urban Genesis to raise capital.
3. **Automated Education Flows**
   - Current: Austin gives manual, high-touch tours.
   - Requirement: A system that triggers short educational videos based on the user's "State of Mastery." As they progress, new content unlocks automatically to reduce 1-on-1 time.
4. **Formalized Auditing System**
   - Current: Users managing funds prove their responsibility via Google Sheets or Forum posts.
   - Requirement: Internalize this process. Build a formal tracking system within the app where Fund Managers must log/audit their deployment of capital.

**Known Bugs**

- **Onboarding Error:** During the demo, the "update_password" step was not marked as "current" for the Fundraiser user type.

**BA Action Items (Deliverables for Next Meeting)** **Do NOT ask the client about:** His current team size, his business model, what payment gateway he uses, or if he starts from scratch (he doesn't).

**Tasks:**

1. **Review the Recording:** Watch the demo meticulously to understand the current UI/UX flow and technical constraints.
2. **Create Understanding Document:** Develop a Mind Map and Solution Flow Diagram that visualizes the current ecosystem (Investor vs. Fundraiser flows) and where the new features (Automation/White-labeling) would plug in.
3. **Prepare Discovery Questions:** Since the roadmap cannot be built yet, prepare a list of deep-dive technical questions to fill the information gaps. Focus specifically on:
   - Edge cases for the $50k transaction limit.
   - Data structures needed for the new Audit Formalization module.
   - Customization limitations for the White-label portals.

name: AI Scheduling - Stephanie
desc:
**Client Overview:** Stephanie is a BCBA therapist and owner of S-cubed, a Flutter-based platform for ABA (Applied Behavior Analysis) clinics. She is looking to scale the platform by integrating AI to handle heavy administrative burdens. She is highly concerned about system stability and wants a methodical, phased rollout.

**Core Requirements:**

- **AI Session Summarization:** Build an AI engine to ingest "pinpoint data" and therapist narratives to generate "compliance-ready" session notes. Must adhere to varying state and insurance regulations.

## **Problem Statement**

Gatehouse, a property development firm with projects across Canada and the U.S., aims to gain a competitive edge in identifying **off-market real estate opportunities** before they reach public listings or traditional brokers.

Their vision is to create an **AI-based property discovery platform** capable of scanning and aggregating property data from multiple public and semi-public sources (MLS, Zillow, property databases, etc.) to locate **specific property types** that meet certain business criteria.

The system should help Gatehouse:

- Discover **undervalued or unlisted properties** that last appeared on MLS 15–20 years ago and haven’t been re-listed.
- Focus on **property owners nearing retirement age**, who may be open to selling or partnership opportunities.
- **Bypass brokers and middlemen** to negotiate directly with owners.
- Generate a **structured, searchable list of leads** with property and ownership details.

The end goal is to provide Gatehouse with **early access to high-value properties** (e.g., trailer parks, car washes, land for development) across business-friendly U.S. states — specifically **Florida, Texas, and Tennessee** — allowing proactive outreach and deal creation.

---

## 🧠 **Functional Requirements**

### 1. **Data Sources & Integration**

- Integrate with multiple **real estate data platforms**:
  - **MLS (Multiple Listing Service)**
  - **Zillow**
  - **Other public or regional property listing sources**
- Extract property data including:
  - Property address, type, previous listing date(s)
  - Ownership records (if available)
  - Current status (listed/unlisted)
  - Contact or tax mailing information (where permissible)
- Include **filters and parameters** for:
  - Properties listed **15–20 years ago** but **not re-listed since**
  - Specific **property categories** (e.g., trailer parks, car washes, undeveloped land)
  - **Geographic scope:** initially limited to **Florida, Texas, and Tennessee**

### 2. **Search & Filtering Engine**

- Build an internal search function allowing:
  - Dynamic filters (date range, state, property type)
  - Natural-language-style queries (optional future enhancement)
- Optionally employ **Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)** for natural query interpretation:
  - Example: “Show me trailer parks in Texas not listed since 2008.”
- Generate result lists with detailed property records.

### 3. **Data Output & Updates**

- Output property lists in structured format:
  - CSV / Excel export
  - API or dashboard view
- Include metadata:
  - Property name/address
  - Year last listed
  - Owner details (if public)
  - Source (MLS, Zillow, etc.)
- **Automated refresh cycle** (monthly or quarterly) to re-run filters and update the dataset.

### 4. **AI/Automation Layer**

- While AI is not central to the initial MVP, apply **AI for automation and enrichment**, such as:
  - Parsing and cleaning heterogeneous data sources
  - Deduplication and normalization of property data
  - Potential future enhancement: predictive scoring of “likely-to-sell” properties based on age, region, and ownership history.

name: HIRECLOUT - A
desc:
## **Problem Statement**

The current recruitment process is highly manual and inefficient, with recruiters spending significant time performing repetitive tasks such as searching for candidates on LinkedIn Recruiter, sending outreach messages, and following up. Despite having a substantial in-house database of 100K candidates (projected to grow to ~600K by November), it remains underutilized due to clunky search capabilities and lack of automation, causing continued over-reliance on LinkedIn Recruiter. This leads to high license costs, inconsistent follow-up, and lost opportunities to engage with qualified candidates already in the system. The goal is to automate sourcing, outreach, and follow-up processes, prioritize internal database usage, and centralize workflows so recruiters can focus on high-value activities such as interviewing and client engagement.

---

## **Requirements (From Prospect Call)**

1. **Candidate Search & Filtering**
   - Ability to search both LinkedIn Recruiter and the internal candidate database.
   - Support for AI / prompt-based filtering (e.g., “Show me active candidates in LA region who we have contacted in the last 6 months”).
   - Automatically identify top 20 candidates for each role.
2. **Candidate Outreach**
   - Automated sending of initial messages to identified candidates.
   - Follow-up messages sent after 3 days if no reply (option for additional touchpoints).
3. **Candidate Activation**
   - Bulk communication to the 600K candidates to determine interest and activity.
   - Categorize/tag candidates as “active” or “inactive” based on responses.
   - Goal: Narrow 600K candidates to an engaged subset (~50K).
4. **Workflow Centralization**
   - Reduce manual recruiter actions (“clicking buttons” on LinkedIn).
   - Centralize tasks so recruiters only engage with candidates who respond positively.
5. **Ownership & Build**
   - Platform must be fully custom-built.
   - All intellectual property belongs to the client.
6. **Database Reliance**
   - Prioritize searching and engaging candidates from the internal database over LinkedIn.
   - LinkedIn to be used with fewer licenses, only as supplemental sourcing.

---

## **Current Manual Workflow vs. Target Automated Workflow**

**Current Manual Workflow:**

1. Recruiter logs into LinkedIn Recruiter.
2. Runs manual searches using filters/keywords from job description.
3. LinkedIn generates candidate list.
4. Recruiter manually sends messages to candidates.
5. Waits for responses (sometimes follows up, sometimes not).
6. If candidate responds, recruiter coordinates screening interview.
7. Selects top candidates to send to client.

**Target Automated Workflow:**

1. Job role entered into system.
2. System searches **internal database** first, then LinkedIn Recruiter (if needed).
3. AI/prompt-based filtering applied to identify best-fit candidates.
4. System selects top 20 candidates automatically.
5. System sends initial personalized outreach message to each candidate.
6. If no reply after 3 days, system sends automated follow-up messages.
7. Candidates who respond positively are flagged as “active” and assigned to recruiters.
8. Recruiter conducts interview with engaged candidates only.

name: DISH - C
desc:
### **Problem Statement:**

DISH currently lacks a real-time system to track the movement and location of physical assets (approx. 75,000+ items) across various facilities. This leads to:

- Inaccurate geolocation data in financial systems.
- Incorrect property tax filings and audits.
- Delayed asset visibility (data may be 1–6 months old).
- Heavy reliance on manual audits and site visits.
- No RFID, barcode scanning, or centralized visibility.
- Existing systems like ServiceNow are only used by IT, covering ~20% of assets.

## **Goals / Outcomes:**

- Enable **real-time asset location tracking** across data centers.
- Eliminate dependency on manual updates and site visits.
- Reduce incorrect property tax payments by ensuring accurate asset location.
- Improve internal transparency and reporting for asset usage and movement.
- Provide scalable architecture that can eventually expand to 200+ facilities.

## **Business Requirements:**

1. **Track Real-Time Location of Assets:**
   - Capture asset transfers between locations (e.g., from Bluffdale, UT to Gilbert, AZ).
   - Show rack-level asset visibility in data centers (Cheyenne & Gilbert to start).
2. **Minimize Manual Data Entry:**
   - Remove need for spreadsheets or emailed updates.
   - Automatically log movement data when assets are physically moved.
3. **Flexible & Scalable:**
   - Must support 30,000 assets initially (in 2 facilities).
   - Scalable to all 75,000+ assets and ~215 nationwide locations.
4. **Cost Efficiency Justification:**
   - Support a business case: system cost (~$200K) vs. projected tax savings & reduced labor.
   - Ability to generate usage reports for ROI tracking.
5. **Internal Presentation Package:**
   - Proposal deck, architecture diagram, business case (TCO/ROI), and timeline for VP approval.

## **Technical Requirements:**

### Phase 1: System Setup for Cheyenne, WY and Gilbert, AZ

1. **Asset Registry Integration:**
   - Use existing **serial number** tracking (not asset tags).
   - Optional: support for future RFID/barcode integration.
2. **Real-Time Geomapping:**
   - Assign geolocation (and rack position) to each asset.
   - Automatically update when assets are moved.
   - No manual triggers (e.g., email updates) required.
3. **Data Center Rack Mapping:**
   - Visual interface showing rack layouts and asset positions.
   - Flag when assets go offline or are physically removed.
4. **Integration with ServiceNow (Optional, IT Only):**
   - If feasible, pull or sync IT asset data with ServiceNow.
   - Non-IT gear (80%) to be managed via new system.
5. **Backend Architecture:**
   - Central database to track all assets.
   - Asset schema: `Serial No, Location, Rack ID, Asset Type, Status, Timestamp`
   - System logs for movement history.
6. **Access Control & Permissions:**
   - Role-based access (Admins, Viewers, Engineers).
   - Support for audit trail/reporting.
7. **Offline to Online Sync (Optional):**
   - In case of offline tracking, system should sync changes once online.
8. **User Dashboard:**
   - Search by asset, serial, location.
   - Reports on moved assets, location mismatches, and audit readiness.

## **Additional Notes:**

- **Standardization varies**: Equipment types differ across racks and locations.
- **RFID Tagging**: May be added if there is a need and we need to suggest this as well if this is required or not.
- **Data entry bottlenecks**: Need to reduce reliance on manual logging and engineers.
- **Deployment Model**: Cloud-based or on-prem (to be finalized based on DISH preference).
- **Timeline Sensitivity**: No hard deadline, but faster delivery = faster executive buy-in.

desc:
## Problem Statement: Little Kitchen Academy (LKA)

Little Kitchen Academy is a growing education brand offering hands-on culinary experiences for children through physical locations. They currently use **Amelia** as their registration platform, which is deeply limiting their customer experience, operational efficiency, and long-term scalability.

They are actively seeking a **custom technology solution** to replace and eventually surpass their current toolset — ideally a phased solution starting with registration + reporting and expanding to a full tech stack including mobile apps and white-label potential.

---

## Key Problems

### 1. **Inefficient Registration Process**

- Users are redirected from LKA’s branded website to Amelia’s platform, breaking the brand experience.
- The registration flow is clunky, multi-click, and difficult to navigate.
- Filters and scheduling views are limited or non-intuitive.
- Customization of terms like “registration” vs. “enrollment” is restricted and expensive.

### 2. **Weak Reporting & Insights**

- Amelia uses Power BI for reporting, but dashboards are underdeveloped.
- Extracting data requires significant manual effort.
- No real-time view into metrics like class enrollment, instructor hours, or seasonal trends.

### 3. **Lack of Customization**

- Changes to class structures, terminology, or user roles require Amelia-side changes.
- Platform is not built for dynamic updates or internal control.
- Gift cards, discount codes, and upsell functionality are limited and hardcoded.

### 4. **No Integrated Mobile Experience**

- No current parent-facing or instructor-facing mobile apps.
- App functionality (scheduling, communication, alerts, etc.) is a major priority post-funding.

---

## Solution Requirements

### Core Web Platform

- **Custom registration system** with seamless, on-site experience.
- Advanced filters (e.g., age, day, time, location) with "Amazon-style" one-click UX.
- Fully branded with no redirects to third-party URLs.
- Support for gift cards, discount codes, add-ons, recurring and one-time payments.
- Admin control over terminology, age groups, pricing, and workflows.

### Dashboards & Reporting

- Real-time, visual dashboards for key KPIs:
  - Class registration by location/age/time
  - Instructor hours
  - Seasonality trends
- Exportable reports, preferably with drag-and-drop builder or low-code config.
- Ability to schedule automated reports.

### Mobile Applications (Not a must have but imp)

- **Parent-facing app:**
  - Schedule/view classes, receive notifications, manage profile, make payments.
- **Instructor-facing app:**
  - View shift schedule, track certifications, receive updates, message staff.

### Tech Stack Ownership & White-Label Potential

- Fully custom stack owned by LKA with IP rights.
- Designed for multi-tenancy (supporting white-label instances for other enrichment brands).
- Scalable infrastructure to support growing number of franchises/locations.

---

## Platforms to Study (To include the features and functionalities)

## Need roadmap and process diagram and architecture diagram on this.

**Problem Statement**

The current caregiver management systems in smaller group home assisted living facilities lack seamless automation and real-time monitoring, leading to inefficiencies in patient care, scheduling, and administrative oversight. Manual processes increase the risk of miscommunication, missed tasks, and limited visibility for facility administrators.

The **Automated Caregiver Platform (ACP)** aims to address these issues by integrating smart home devices, providing real-time monitoring, streamlining caregiver workflows, and ensuring secure remote access for administrators. The platform will be cost-effective, lightweight, and internally managed to reduce reliance on external IT support.

## **Technical Requirements**

### **1. System Architecture & Infrastructure**

- Cloud-based or hybrid deployment model for scalability.
- Secure database for storing patient data, schedules, and device logs.
- API-based integration with smart home devices.
- HIPAA-compliant security measures, including encryption and access controls.

### **2. Smart Device Integration**

- **Cameras:** Live-streaming with secure, role-based access.
- **Thermostat:** Real-time temperature monitoring and remote adjustments.
- **Smart Doors (Front & Garage):** Secure access with logging and remote control.
- **IoT Device Hub:** Synchronization of all connected devices with the platform.

### **3. Caregiver Scheduling & Task Management**

- Calendar-based scheduling for caregivers (daily/weekly).
- Task assignment and tracking with real-time status updates.
- Notification system for reminders and pending tasks.

desc:
### Problem Statement

The core issue centers around inefficiencies in connecting seniors to suitable care facilities, balancing complex datasets, HIPAA compliance, and optimizing customer experience. The current manual processes for gathering information, evaluating care needs, and matching seniors with appropriate facilities are time-consuming and labor-intensive. This impacts both the business's scalability and the quality of service provided to seniors and their families.
So, the prospect wants to automate the process to decrease the time to touch for his process to increase efficiency.

**Key Requirements (**Process Automation**)**

1. **Automated Data Collection**:
   - Implement **speech-to-text transcription** to extract actionable data from family/patient conversations.
   - Develop a **form builder tool** that collects static and dynamic patient data, including care plans, preferences, and financials.
   - Ensure that the data collection process complies with **HIPAA** and financial privacy regulations.
2. **Data Integration and Processing**:
   - Create a **centralized data repository** for managing patient profiles, facility information, and static data fields.
   - Develop an **AI algorithm** to match patient profiles with suitable facilities based on preferences, care needs, and financial constraints.
   - Enable cross-referencing of patient needs with **real-time facility availability** if available or prompt updates when occupancy changes.
3. **Communication Automation**:
   - Integrate with tools like **Twilio** for automated email and SMS communication with facility managers.
   - Automatically send patient profiles and care plans to relevant facilities, emphasizing alignment with their capabilities.
4. **Scheduling and Follow-Up**:
   - Include a **tour scheduling feature** to coordinate visits between families and facilities.
   - Automate follow-ups for updates on patient placement or additional care requirements.
5. **Reporting and Analytics**:
   - Generate detailed **reports** summarizing placement activity, success rates, and time-to-placement metrics.
   - Provide analytics to predict facility vacancies and identify trends in senior care needs.

---

### Current Business Operation Process Flow (Pre-Automation)

#### **1. Patient Referral and Initial Contact**

- **Input**:
  - Referral from a case manager, discharge nurse, or family member.
  - Communication via text, email, or phone call.
- **Action**:
  - Placement agent receives notification of a patient requiring placement, including basic details (e.g., discharge date, care plan).
  - Agent reaches out to the patient or family for additional information.

#### **2. Data Collection**

- **Input**:
  - Family/patient interview (phone or in-person).
  - Assessment form sent to families for detailed information (optional).
- **Action**:
  - Placement agent manually collects patient information such as:
    - Care requirements (e.g., skilled nursing, therapy needs).
    - Lifestyle preferences (e.g., amenities, dietary restrictions).
    - Financial constraints (budget and insurance details).
  - Data is entered into spreadsheets or other manual tools.

#### **3. Facility Search and Match**

- **Input**:
  - Patient profile created from collected data.
  - Static facility data stored in Word documents or spreadsheets.
- **Action**:
  - Placement agent manually filters facilities based on:
    - Location preferences.
    - Care plan alignment.
    - Lifestyle and amenity match.
  - Agent cross-references facility availability (e.g., open beds) by:
    - Sending broadcast emails to community managers.
    - Calling individual facilities to check occupancy and suitability.

#### **4. Communication with Facilities**

- **Input**:
  - Patient profile.
  - Selected facilities based on manual search.
- **Action**:
  - Placement agent prepares emails or calls facilities to share patient details.
  - Facility managers respond with availability and potential fit.
  - Scheduling tours or visits, if necessary.

#### **5. Patient Placement**

- **Input**:
  - Facility responses and availability confirmations.
  - Finalized patient preferences and care plan.
- **Action**:
  - Placement agent coordinates with the family to visit and select a facility.
  - Final placement decision is made.
  - Agent confirms placement with the facility and schedules move-in date.

#### **6. Post-Placement Follow-Up**

- **Input**:
  - Feedback from families and facilities.
  - Ongoing care updates (if required).
- **Action**:
  - Agent collects reviews and referrals.
  - Reviews process performance for improvement opportunities.

---

### **Problem Statement**

HustlePay aims to address high checkout abandonment rates by enabling merchants to accept multiple payment methods seamlessly. Most merchants rely on a single-payment method, limiting consumer flexibility. HustlePay provides an API-driven solution that allows consumers to split payments across various sources—credit cards, BNPL, digital wallets (PayPal, CashApp, Venmo), government checks, store credit, and cryptocurrency—while optimizing transaction routing through integrated payment processors.

### **Requirements**

#### **1. API Architecture Development**

- Develop a scalable API framework to support multi-source payment processing.
- Ensure jurisdiction-agnostic payment routing to local and global processors.

#### **2. Continuous Integration of Payment Methods**

- Implement onboarding workflows for credit cards, BNPL, PayPal, CashApp, Venmo, gift cards, cryptocurrencies, and government checks.
- Develop a merchant web app for KYB data collection and agreement execution.
- Enable ERP integration for automated merchant onboarding and discount calculation.

#### **3. Scalable Framework and Testing**

- Design a modular system that accommodates new features with minimal disruption.
- Implement a comprehensive testing environment for performance and security validation.

#### **4. Consumer and Wallet Integration**

- Build APIs for Apple Wallet, Google Wallet, and merchant apps.
- Develop a consumer app to manage payments and optimize checkout.

#### **5. AI-Driven Optimization**

- Use machine learning for optimal payment routing.
- Implement real-time transaction analysis and fraud detection.

#### **6. ERP Integration and Plugin Design**

- Develop a plugin that acts as a bridge between ERP systems and HustlePay’s API.
- Ensure ERP integration supports WooCommerce initially, with future expansion to Magento.
- Sync transaction data to provide insights for better payment processing options.

#### **7. Transaction Routing and Splitting**

- Enable invoice splitting based on jurisdiction, transaction size, and abandonment risk.
- Ensure seamless rollback mechanisms for failed transactions to prevent payment mismatches.

#### **8. Checkout Widget Development**

- Enable the widget to complete payments within an ERP.
- Support multiple payment categories (credit card, BNPL, PayPal, gift card).
- Dynamically integrate third-party payment widgets using API keys.
- Track, record, and sync multiple payments within the ERP system.

#### **9. Security and Compliance**

- Implement PCI-DSS-compliant data encryption and handling policies.

#### **10. Merchant Admin Portal**

- Allow merchants to configure payment options, view payment statistics, and manage agreements.
- Provide visibility into processing volume and negotiate better merchant rates.

---

### **Deliverables**

1. **API framework** supporting multi-source payments.
2. **Checkout widget** integrating multiple payment options.
3. **Merchant admin portal** for configuration and reporting.
4. **ERP plugin** to sync transactions and optimize processing.
5. **Security and compliance** measures for secure payment handling.
6. **AI-powered optimization** for dynamic payment routing.

desc:
(Ahmad Khalid was with me on the call as well)

## Problem Statement

**The client, a home care services provider operating since 2008, is seeking to modernize and streamline its end-to-end operations using AI-driven automation.**

Currently, their processes — from client onboarding to care scheduling and caregiver hiring — involve significant manual effort, fragmented tools, and duplicated data entry. This not only leads to inefficiencies and delays but also increases the risk of errors and limits scalability.

A critical obstacle is the lack of a seamless, intelligent integration between external AI tools (e.g., voice assistants, schedulers, transcription engines) and their core system, **WellSky Personal Care**, which acts as the operational hub for scheduling, case management, and records.

# Technical Brief: AI-Driven Workflow Automation

## Overview

We are preparing a custom solution for a home care services provider aiming to leverage AI to streamline client onboarding, scheduling, hiring, and integration with their existing CRM: **WellSky Personal Care**. The goal is to **minimize human interaction**, automate repetitive tasks, and **seamlessly integrate** with WellSky through its API.

---

## Core Modules to Build

### 1. **Lead Intake & Contact Capture**

- **Input Channels**: Email, phone call (voice-to-text transcription), SMS, web forms, and social channels (e.g., FB, LinkedIn).
- **Required Data to Extract/Store**:
  - First name, last name
  - Phone number, email
  - Preferred contact method
  - Problem/situation summary (e.g., “Mother fell and now can’t be home alone”)
- **Processing**:
  - Auto-create a **contact record** in WellSky via API.

---

### 2. **Case Routing & Coordinator Assignment**

- **Logic for Assignment**:
  - Match problem category to an available **care coordinator** (from existing staff pool).
  - Optionally use skill-based routing and availability checks.
- **AI Functionality**:
  - Care coordinator is assigned automatically.
  - Notifications are sent to care coordinator with client details and issue summary.
- **Note**: The client does _not_ want the care coordinator reaching out manually.

---

### 3. **Registered Nurse Scheduling**

- **Coordinator Action**:
  - After reviewing case details, the coordinator chooses an appropriate **Registered Nurse** (RN) from a system-generated list.
  - Assignment is logged in system and **pushed to WellSky** under the client record.
- **Client Scheduling**:
  - RN’s calendar is sent to the client.
  - Client self-selects a time.
  - System sends calendar invites to both RN and client.
  - Add buffer rules (no double booking, minimum advance time, etc.).

---

### 4. **Intake Assessment Automation**

- **Meeting Type**: Virtual or phone (recorded).
- **AI/NLP Use**:
  - Transcribe meeting between RN and client.
  - Extract structured data from transcription.
  - Auto-populate **WellSky Intake Form** from this data.
  - Format should match WellSky’s schema (field validation, input types, etc.).
- **Compliance**:
  - Ensure all PII/PHI in this workflow is HIPAA-compliant.
  - Securely store raw audio, transcriptions, and forms.
  - Encrypt sensitive fields at rest and in transit.

---

### 5. **Caregiver Hiring Workflow**

> (Currently mid-stream on this; we’re extending/streamlining further.)

- **Automation Goals**:
  - Transcription of the conversation by the Care Co-ordinator with the Care Giver needs to be saved in the WellSky as well. This step can be further automated but at the later stage.

---

### 6. **WellSky Integration**

- **API Strategy**:
  - All contacts, cases, appointments, assessments, and intake forms must be pushed into WellSky in real-time.
  - Use WellSky’s **API Connect** to perform the following:
    - `POST /contacts`
    - `PUT /intake`
    - `GET /staff/availability`
    - `POST /appointment`
    - `PATCH /care_plan`

---

### 7. **Data Security & HIPAA Compliance**

- **Must-Haves**:
  - All PHI data must be encrypted.
  - Only authorized staff may access sensitive data.
  - Transcriptions and audio recordings stored with audit trails.

name: RGB - J
desc:
### **Problem Statement**

RGB currently operates its production pipeline using a series of **Excel spreadsheets and macros**, developed over 20+ years by a single internal expert. These macros automate key workflows across departments including sales, engineering, detailing, and manufacturing. However, the system is becoming increasingly unstable due to **Windows security updates** and lack of support, causing critical programs to fail unexpectedly.

The current setup:

- Relies heavily on **manual processes**
- Is **highly fragile** due to single-user dependency and lack of documentation
- Involves **redundant data entry** across 8+ internal tools
- Cannot be reliably maintained post-retirement of the current owner

RGB is seeking to replace this fragile and outdated system with a **custom-built, web-based platform** that consolidates and streamlines their core production workflows in a robust, user-friendly, and future-proof manner.
They currently store everything on-premis servers.

### **Technical Requirements for the New Web-Based Platform**

#### 1. **Architecture & Platform**

- **Web-based application** (browser-accessible)
- Must be **independent of Windows OS** (no reliance on Excel/macros/VBA)
- Built using modern, maintainable frameworks.
- Self-hosted or cloud-hosted with full ownership by RGB

#### 2. **Core Functional Modules**

Each of the following modules reflects one of the legacy tools/processes currently used:

- **Job Intake & BOM Management**
  - Ingests **design output** (Bill of Materials) from **MDS software**
  - Supports parsing and standardizing BOM for use in downstream modules
  - Handles both standard and custom parts
- **Estimate vs. Design (EVD) Module**
  - Compares sales estimates with finalized engineering designs
  - Displays cost variance and flags discrepancies
  - Allows manual override or adjustment
- **Detailing Interface**
  - Enables detailing department to define part-specific data
  - Supports 80+ data input fields/tabs (equivalent to current e-shipper setup)
  - Handles logic for part fabrication instructions (holes, bends, material type, colors, etc.)
- **Shipper/Logistics Builder**
  - Aggregates finalized part data into “shippers” for transport
  - Organizes components by weld sets, accessories, fasteners, etc.
  - Outputs clean **CSV files** to be sent to the shop floor systems
- **Purchasing Module**
  - Generates pre-release material lists from BOM
  - Supports lead time and raw material requirements
  - Not connected to ERP; generates internal data for procurement team

#### 3. **Data Model & Storage**

- Centralized, normalized **relational database**
- Must support:
  - Job-level tracking (unique job ID)
  - Part-level specs
  - Quantity breakdowns
  - Variant configurations (color, coatings, etc.)

#### 4. **User Roles & Interfaces**

- Role-based access (Engineering, Detailing, Sales, Admin)
- Interfaces tailored per department
- Lightweight, fast-loading, and designed for internal teams with minimal training

#### 5. **Data Import/Export**

- Import from MDS (likely structured file formats – confirm JSON, XML, or CSV)
- Export as CSV for downstream use (e.g., shop floor machinery, external tools)
- No ERP integration required

#### 6. **Scalability & Maintainability**

- Modular design to accommodate future enhancements
- Well-documented codebase and business logic
- Flexible enough to accommodate ~200 unique parts per job and large volume variations (small to very large buildings)

#### 7. **Support for Complex Fabrication Logic**

- Rules-based part processing (e.g., galvanization, unique welds, accessories)
- Allow for part-specific exceptions and overrides
- Needs to replicate nuanced rules currently buried in Excel macros

#### 8. **Collaboration with Existing Expert**

- Platform development must include direct collaboration with the current system owner (the retiring prospect)
- He will assist with **spec writing**, rule definitions, testing, and validation
